blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff, §§9.2 and 12.3; North Star scope
blocking.problem: The proposal changes certificate layout and root identity without stating how a mixed fat object uses them. Neither the note nor INDEX's shared publication decisions identifies the embedded device object as the binding subject or explains certificate inventory alongside native host code. This fails the council's explicit standing mixed-fat-object check, independently of the otherwise sound applicability repair.
blocking.fix: Append to §12.3: 'A mixed fat object may contain native host code together with embedded ISA objects and certificates for their oracle or action roots. Each certificate's object_hash binds its embedded ISA object; interface_hash, closure_hash and reference_program_hash identify the selected device root under §9.2. The fat-object container associates each certificate with that embedded object and root closure, and a composed certificate retains linked device proof records under their owner closure hashes. Native host code outside the tainted call graph remains native and is not required to appear as ISA regions or carry oracle comparison claims or fault censuses.' This permits a container inventory or separate per-root packets; I would use separate per-root packets associated by object and root closure hashes.

suggestions: In §12.3, repeat the existing preflight timing explicitly: 'Before any effect of the enclosing CC/R region call, validate coverage for every transitively executed qinplace using its resolved token and arguments.' The existing §4.5 rule remains binding; the new phrase 'at every reached instruction' should not suggest delaying validation until after earlier gates have executed.

In the alternatives table, replace 'Put all nested proofs in the outer packet' with 'Put nested inverse_pairs entries and their claims in the outer region record'. A single composed outer packet containing regions[closure(inner)] is valid and is precisely the transport arrangement the recommended diff permits.
path_to_accept: Add the mixed-fat-object binding and inventory statement in 0JQ-1 to the exact §12.3 diff. The remaining changes are editorial suggestions; no core repair is required.
summary: The main defect statements, clause references, H algebra, inverse-pair ownership and conditional hash/catalog claims check out. The proposal needs one contract addition to satisfy the mandatory mixed-fat-object check.
